Popivtsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews are believed to have lived in Popivtsi from the 17th century; between 1882 and 1903 the town was closed to new Jewish settlers, though by 1914 Jews owned the only pharmaceutical store, both grocers, and all four manufacturing shops. Following the German-Romanian occupation and 1941 annexation to Transnistria, about 1,000 Jews were brought from Bessarabia and Bukovina, most perishing alongside the local community; around 800 died of cold, starvation, and disease during the winter of 1941–42 alone. This cemetery, apparently established in the 18th century, holds about 500 gravestones dating from the late 19th to 20th centuries.
